extracted.intended_audience: Military Sealift Command managers, Navy contracting officers, naval logistics and procurement policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment of OMB Circular A-76 application to Military Sealift Command (MSC) Nucleus Fleet operations, focusing on cost, readiness, maintenance quality, statements of work, and quality assurance implementation. Intended to inform MSC managers and contracting personnel on problems, requirements, and recommended QA practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 cost savings threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 specifies that a commercial contractor replaces an in-house operation only if the contractor's bid provides at least a 10 percent savings over the in-house bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if MSC does not bid below its pre-bid operating budget, the contractor replacing an in-house operation must do so at a cost savings of at least 10 percent. Interviews suggest contractors often achieve substantially more than 10% savings through manning reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive fixed-price bidding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Government organizations and commercial contractors submit fixed-price bids for the right to perform services; the lowest-priced, capable commercial source wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A government organization that loses an A-76 bid competition is dismantled and its workers reassigned or laid off. This mechanism is a fundamental feature of A-76 and shapes organizational and personnel consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance work statement (SOW) control
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of work includes performance standards for specified tasks and financial penalties for contractors whose performance falls below those standards; contractors and government organizations are free to perform the work in any safe manner consistent with government demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies or ambiguities in the SOW lead to contractors refusing tasks not specified or charging high prices for them. SOW completeness is critical to ensure required maintenance and services are performed without dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of MSC minimum maintenance standards in SOW
rubrics_metrics.description: MSC minimum maintenance standards must be specified in the SOW; omission prevents QA supervisors from determining whether maintenance performed satisfies MSC's minimum requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although SOWs instruct contractors to comply with U.S. Coast Guard regulations and American Bureau of Shipping rules, MSC's own minimum maintenance standards were omitted and should be explicitly included to enable measurement and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Level (QAL) and QASP implementation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 mandates that the government implement Quality Assurance or Quality Control programs; Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs) must be established and implemented by the Area Commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP policy must be fair, reasonable, and equitable, not dependent on perceived contractor 'quality', and similar to MSC's QC plan for retained vessels. Lack of timely QA standards and guidance undermined inspectors' ability to establish contractor QA levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventive maintenance inspection and sampling procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For preventive maintenance, each piece of equipment is considered an element of the lot from which samples will be drawn; sampled elements will be inspected, test operated, and machinery history cards reviewed for documentation of required maintenance actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluator's rating should reflect a composite of inspection, operation tests, and records review, noting general equipment condition and appraising contractor performance. Unsatisfactory ratings will be somewhat subjective but should allow shipboard managers to program and prioritize maintenance actions without being penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor repairs sampling and inspection schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor repairs are managed by compiling a list from a joint walk-through for three quarters of the year to be evaluated by random sampling during quarterly inspections; during the pre-overhaul quarter a 100% checklist inspection is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific repairs required to maintain acceptable material readiness must be performed immediately, otherwise they remain on the outstanding list. The level of inspection detail must be similar to that used for MSC-operated ships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor insurance requirement (P&I coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor shall secure the customary full-form Protection and Indemnity (P&I) marine insurance coverage to cover all liabilities in the amount of $100 million per incident; the contractor is responsible for the cost, including deductibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual premiums vary by ship type (examples given for oceanographic ships). Historically, when the federal government acted as insurer no premium was required; current contracts place insurance cost burden on contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of Coast Guard requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When industry minimums and Coast Guard minimums differ, Coast Guard requirements take precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFPs recommended elimination of all positions over the required industry or Coast Guard minimum; where these minimums differ, Coast Guard requirements govern staffing and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of contract administration costs in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 cost comparison guidelines address contract administration costs in detail and such administrative costs should be included in assessing the full cost of contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting may involve additional administrative costs (additional contract administrators or use of military personnel in unauthorized billets). The report recommends developing procedures to determine full cost impact including MSC Engineering, Operations, and Personnel staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for measuring in-house contract performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported criterion for measuring MSC in-house contract performance is maintaining ships' operational status while sustaining the maintenance quality level that existed prior to A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appears to diverge from A-76 procedures that provide specific, measurable criteria for contractors; MSC's lack of quantification of in-house preventive maintenance complicates comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor obligation limited to SOW tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor is not required to perform tasks omitted from the SOW and can refuse or demand additional fees for additional maintenance not included in the SOW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In contrast, MSC in-house operations have been reported to perform maintenance not included in their SOW without expectation of additional resources. Remedy: amend SOW to include preventive maintenance and minor repair tasks as specified in MSC QA program.

rubrics_metrics.name: QASP policy principles: fairness, equity, similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP implementation policy should be fair and reasonable, equitable in application (not dependent on the contractor's perceived 'quality'), and similar to the Quality Control plan to be implemented by MSC for retained vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASPs must include requirements for interaction with the contractor using his Quality Control plan; MSC cannot avoid establishing surveillance programs that cover performance in all areas as integral to A-76.
